public_rationale: AISLE's tests for the April 7–9, 2026 announcement period support the qualified claim. Given isolated relevant code, all eight tested models, including several open-weight models, identified the FreeBSD vulnerability. GPT-OSS-120b also recovered the core OpenBSD chain [e1]. This demonstrates substantial vulnerability analysis in the simplified setting [e1]. None reproduced Mythos's specific multi-round RPC delivery method, and the proposed alternatives were not executed [e2].
limitations: No independent rerun was verified in the evidence packet.
The tests do not establish autonomous discovery or successful end-to-end exploitation [e2].
The April 9 update reported frequent false positives on patched code, limiting conclusions about practical reliability [e2].

statement.document_title: Three reasons to think that the Claude Mythos announcement from Anthropic was overblown

from_speaker: can already do a fair amount
our_interpretation: The surrounding quotation identifies the task as recovering vulnerability analysis from isolated code taken from Anthropic's showcases.

The plain reading is that available open-weight models can reproduce substantial useful analysis in that simplified setting. It does not require autonomous discovery across a repository or a working exploit.
The target period is the announcement and immediate response, April 7–9, 2026. This is the latest publicly observable state before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Published tests show open-weight models recovering substantial vulnerability identification, causal analysis, or exploitability reasoning for the showcased cases when given the relevant code.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable isolated-code tests show that open-weight models generally cannot recover substantive analysis, or that the reported successes do not identify the actual vulnerabilities.
